prompt: Given a list of time ranges, merge all overlapping ranges.
why: Sort by start; extend the last merged range or start a new one.
trap: Union-find can group overlaps but needs O(n²) comparisons to find them.

prompt: Insert a new interval into a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals, merging where needed.
why: Copy those that end before it, merge those that overlap, copy the rest. One sweep.
trap: Binary search finds where it goes, but you still have to sweep to merge.

prompt: Given meeting times, can one person attend all of the meetings?
why: Sort by start and check whether any meeting starts before the previous one ends.
trap: Counting rooms needs a heap; a yes/no for one person just needs the sorted sweep.

prompt: Each employee has a list of busy intervals. Find the common free time for everyone.
why: Pool and sort all busy intervals, merge them, and the gaps between merged ranges are the free time.
trap: A heap can merge the per-person lists, but the core move is still merging intervals.

prompt: Given two sorted lists of disjoint intervals, return their intersections.
tells: two sorted lists of disjoint intervals
why: Walk both lists; the overlap of the current pair is [max start, min end]; advance whichever ends first.
trap: Two indices move here, but the reasoning is all about interval overlap.
